note:
AMENDMENT (pre-grill, from the adversarial review of the idea set). Four changes:
(1) AC-2 PRESUPPOSES AN AC IDENTITY THE FORMAT FORBIDS. 'An AC named in a transferred.scope' — but scope is declared VERBATIM FREE TEXT (journey-format-spec §3; the writer checks only that it is a string, store.ts:1486) while conclusion() matches ACs by a normalised prefix of the full AC text (commands/index.ts:1499-1501). A non-empty check does not make a concatenated verbatim scope parseable, so the close rule cannot credit anything. AMEND: define the scope's internal shape (one AC per line as '<AC-id>: <text verbatim>') so credit is ID-based, or state that the credit is text-prefix based and amend the read to match.
(2) gate-revised IS NEAR-TAUTOLOGICAL IN THE COMPOSITE. F-AC16 fires BECAUSE gate-revised exists (store.ts:1662) and then demands the transferred event the gesture writes anyway; no AC defines what {old,new} means for a half-accept. AMEND: either drop gate-revised from the composite or define exactly what changed and why it is recorded.
(3) THERE IS NO TRANSACTION, SO STATE THE ORDER AND THE RESUME. 'ONE validated act' is 3-5 sequential appends (gate!'s own shape, commands/index.ts:556-576); AC-1's 'zero writes' covers VALIDATION only. A crash mid-composite leaves a partial closure and neither this task nor 12/13 states the ordering it relies on (the transfer must be recorded before the auto-completed close, or check() may flag the node later). AMEND: state the order and the resume rule (a re-run completes the sequence; no transaction is claimed).
(4) THE CROSS-TASK COUPLINGS ARE UNDECLARED. AC-2's 'the record reads this AC moved to <target>' is a CARD change (src/surface — not in this task's targetAreas), and 12/13's AC-4 depends on 12/11's read. AMEND: declare both couplings in the contract.

DELIVERY NOTE (post-implementation, leg 12/12) — how the two pre-grill amendments were settled, and the couplings a reviewer should look for.

(1) SETTLED — THE SCOPE HAS AN INTERNAL SHAPE. The amendment was right: the format declares `scope` VERBATIM free text, and a verbatim blob is not parseable, so AC-2's credit could not work as written. Rather than break the format's verbatim promise, the convention is defined (in `src/store/transfer.ts`, and recorded in journey-format-spec §3): ONE AC PER LINE, the id first — `AC-2: <the criterion, verbatim>`. The TEXT is the record; the ID is what the close credits. The credit is ID-based, so a line naming no AC is legal and credits NOTHING (residual scope that maps to no criterion is an honest record that simply cannot satisfy one), and a typo'd id would silently credit nothing — which is why `transfer-unknown-ac` refuses at write time. claims[] still wins over a transfer for the same AC (the claim match is tried FIRST in conclusion()).

(2) SETTLED — `gate-revised` IS DROPPED FROM THE COMPOSITE. The format gives that event only a `{old,new}` pair of gate NAMES; a half accept leaves the gate `confirm`, so writing it would record a revision with nothing revised AND arm F-AC16 against a fact the `transferred` event already states. The composite is therefore accept + transfer (+ close), nothing more. AC-1's parenthetical offered `gate-revised` as part of the gesture; this is the answer to why it is not there.

(3) THE SUCCESSOR RIDES THE GATE DECISION, NOT A FIFTH KIND. `DecisionPoint.successor` is set on the accept when a `transferred` event follows it. A fifth kind was rejected because a `transferred` event carries no `why` channel of its own: as its own kind it would read NO WHY RECORDED on every half accept while the reason sits one event earlier on the accept. This is what 12/13's AC-4 ('the transfer with its why') reads.

(4) THE ONE HONEST LIMIT OF AC-2. `closeEvidenceBlocker` — the single close predicate shared by `complete!` and the confirm-accept auto-close — does NOT read `unclaimed`, so the auto-close is NOT what the transfer unlocks (verified empirically against the built CLI before writing this). AC-3 forbids changing that predicate, so the transfer's verifiable effects are the `complete!` refusal and the READS (conclusion · brief · card): a moved AC stops being reported as an owed gap and is named as moved, with its successor. The auto-close behaviour is unchanged, deliberately.

(5) NOTICED, NOT FIXED — `src/flow/intents.ts:150`. The `close` intent's `gate-revised` arm writes `gate: 'confirm'` (a bare string), which the store's shape check refuses (`gate` must be `{old,new}`). Latent and untested, outside AC-1..AC-5 and outside this task's targetAreas; flagged here so it is not lost.

(6) COUPLING DECLARED. AC-2's user-visible half is `src/surface` (brief's TRANSFERRED block, the decision line) — 12/13's targetArea, touched here because the AC names the read; the served UI card is left to 12/13. The engine half (`src/store/transfer.ts`, `src/commands`) is this task's.
